I came back to #36165, which I completely forgot had been delegated 3 months ago – I was notified of the expiring delegation. I updated the PR, but then MathlibTest/EllipticCurve.lean failed. I then fixed it, and then the bors delegation was cancelled.

I have fixed the test. Can someone please merge it as soon as possible?
cc @Bryan Gin-ge Chen, is the delegation supposed to be cancelled when fixing a test?

I don't see the delegation getting canceled on that PR; it looks like you wrote bors merge and then pushed a commit to the branch afterwards which took the PR off the queue (and did this a few times). I guess the message from bors there is a bit confusing since it says "Canceled"; I can try and make that more clear since I'm already hacking on bors.

Bryan Gin-ge Chen said:

I guess the message from bors there is a bit confusing since it says "Canceled"; I can try and make that more clear since I'm already hacking on bors.

Right then, I'd be more than happy if that bors message was clarified

Does maxRecDepth 300 no longer work? I don't particularly care about it but it was added at the request of @Jon Eugster.
Is strongRec' more efficient than strongRec for some reason?

Junyan Xu said:

Is strongRec' more efficient than strongRec for some reason?

Well, see this comment

Junyan Xu said:

Does maxRecDepth 300 no longer work? I don't particularly care about it but it was added at the request of Jon Eugster.

It does kind of defeat the purpose to have a test which "test[s] that the kernel is able to [...] and should be relatively fast" if you don't set any measure what "relatively fast" means. If maxRecDepth is the right tool is another question. But also, I don't think this particular test is important.

However, @Jeremy Tan, when you do modify test files, please try to read them carefully and think about what they tried to capture and if the modification still captures this thruthfully. If tests are just modified without much consideration, it's very easy to make them pointless or to reintroduce bugs which the tests were supposed to guard against. If this was my own PR which edited a test file this way, that would have been reason enough for me to un-delegate the PR and go through another review cycle.
